title.zh: 卷337 列傳一百二十四 卢焯 图尔炳阿 阿思哈 宫兆麟 杨景素 闵鹗元
title.en: Volume 337 Biographies 124: Lu Chao, Tu Er Bing A, A Si Ha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, Min Eyuan
title.raw: 卷337 列傳一百二十四 卢焯 图尔炳阿 阿思哈 宫兆麟 杨景素 闵鹗元

sentences.zh: 列傳一百二十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 124
translations.idiomatic: Biography 124

sentences.zh: 盧焯圖爾炳阿阿思哈宮兆麟楊景素閔鶚元

translations.literal: Lu Chao, Tu Erbing'a, Asiha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, Min Eyuan
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chao, Tu Erbing'a, Asiha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, and Min Eyuan

sentences.zh: 盧焯，字光植，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Lu Chao, courtesy name Guangzhi, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chao, styled Guangzhi, was a Han Chinese bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 入貲授直隸武邑知縣。

translations.literal: By purchase of office he was appointed magistrate of Wuyi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way into office as magistrate of Wuyi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 縣舊有均徭錢供差費，遇差仍按裡派夫，焯革除之，又歸火耗於公，捕盜尤力。

translations.literal: The county had long levied equalized corvée money for dispatch expenses, yet when duties arose labor was still apportioned by li; Chao abolished this. He also remitted surplus grain fees to the public account and was especially vigorous in apprehending bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The county had long collected equalized corvée funds for official errands, yet whenever a duty arose corvée labor was still levied by neighborhood; Chao abolished the practice. He also turned surplus grain fees over to the public treasury and was notably zealous in catching thieves.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，解餉詣京師，世宗特召對。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, while escorting tribute funds to the capital, he received a special audience from the Yongzheng Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728, while delivering tribute silver to the capital, he was granted a special audience by the Yongzheng Emperor.

sentences.zh: 遷江南亳州知州，禁械鬥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Bozhou in Jiangnan and prohibited armed brawls.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Bozhou in Jiangnan, where he banned factional armed fights.

sentences.zh: 再遷山東東昌知府，總督田文鏡遣官弁四出訪事，東昌民逮下獄甚眾，焯至，悉判遣之。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be prefect of Dongchang in Shandong. Governor-general Tian Wenjing had sent officials in all directions to investigate matters, and very many people of Dongchang had been arrested and imprisoned; when Chao arrived, he judged and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made prefect of Dongchang in Shandong. Governor-general Tian Wenjing had sent officers far and wide to investigate cases, and a great many Dongchang residents had been thrown into jail; on taking office, Chao reviewed the cases and released them all.

sentences.zh: 會有水災，焯疏運河，築護城長堤，動帑賑恤。

translations.literal: When flooding occurred, Chao dredged the Grand Canal, built a long protective dike around the city wall, and drew on the treasury for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck, he dredged the Grand Canal, built a long embankment around the city walls, and spent state funds on relief.

sentences.zh: 上遣大臣閱視，獨東昌得完。

translations.literal: The emperor sent grand ministers to inspect; Dongchang alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched high officials to inspect the damage; only Dongchang emerged unscathed.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷督糧道，移河南南汝道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to grain transport intendant and then to the Nannu Circuit in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1731 he was moved to grain transport intendant, then to the Nannu circuit in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十年，授按察使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1732 he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1733 he was promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢福建巡撫，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor of Fujian and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1734 he was elevated to governor of Fujian and awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十三年，高宗即位，焯疏言被水州縣不成災，上諭曰：「被水雖不成災，仍須加意賑恤，毋使小民失所。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Gaozong Emperor acceded; Chao memorialized that flooded prefectures and counties had not become disaster areas. The emperor instructed: 'Though flooding has not become a disaster, you must still give extra care to relief so that the common people do not lose their homes.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1736, when the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Chao reported that flood-hit districts had not technically qualified as disaster areas. The emperor replied: 'Even if the floods have not risen to the level of a declared disaster, you must still relieve the people with special care and keep the poor from losing their livelihoods.'

sentences.zh: 」乾隆元年，請查丈建陽民田，上諭曰：「小民畏查丈如水火。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he requested a survey and remeasurement of civilian fields in Jianyang. The emperor instructed: 'The common people dread surveys and remeasurements as they dread fire and flood.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he asked to survey and remeasure civilian land in Jianyang. The emperor warned: 'Ordinary people fear land surveys as they fear fire and water.'

sentences.zh: 汝初為加賦起見，今又以豁除掩非，一存觀望之心，所謂無一而可也。

translations.literal: At first you acted with an eye to increasing levies; now you use exemptions to cover your errors, always keeping a mind of hesitation—there is nothing here that can be approved.
translations.idiomatic: You began by trying to raise taxes, and now you propose exemptions to cover your mistakes, always hedging your bets—there is nothing in this that I can approve.'

sentences.zh: 」尋奏減邵武永安所、霞浦福寧衛屯田徵米科則，豁閩、侯官諸縣額缺田地。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized to reduce the grain levy rates on garrison fields at Yong'an sub-prefecture in Shaowu and Funing guard in Xiapu, and to exempt shortfall lands in Min, Houguan, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he memorialized to lower grain tax rates on garrison farms at Yong'an in Shaowu and Funing in Xiapu, and to exempt registered shortfall lands in Min, Houguan, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 又以平和、永安、清流諸縣田少丁多，請減免攤餘丁銀。

translations.literal: He also, because Pinghe, Yong'an, Qingliu, and other counties had little land but many adult males, requested reduction or exemption of the apportioned surplus adult-male silver levy.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to reduce or waive the apportioned surplus adult-male tax in Pinghe, Yong'an, Qingliu, and other counties where land was scarce but households were numerous.

sentences.zh: 又奏教民蠶績，疏濬省會城河。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to teach the people sericulture and to dredge the provincial capital's city moat.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed teaching sericulture to the people and dredging the canal around the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，調浙江巡撫，兼鹽政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to governor of Zhejiang, concurrently supervising the salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1738 he was transferred to Zhejiang as governor, with concurrent charge of the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 奏請停仁和、海寧二縣草塘歲修銀，減嘉興屬七縣銀米十之二。

translations.literal: He memorialized to halt the annual repair silver for sod seawalls in Renhe and Haining counties and to reduce grain and silver levies in the seven counties under Jiaxing by two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to suspend annual repair funds for earthen seawalls in Renhe and Haining and to cut grain and silver taxes in Jiaxing's seven subordinate counties by twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 又奏陳鹽政諸事：請禁商人短秤；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on various salt-administration matters: requesting a ban on merchants using short weights;
translations.idiomatic: He also laid out salt-policy reforms: merchants must be forbidden to use short weights;

sentences.zh: 飭州縣捕私鹽毋擾民；

translations.literal: ordering prefectures and counties to seize illicit salt without harassing the people;
translations.idiomatic: prefectural and county officials must seize smuggled salt without harassing the populace;

sentences.zh: 毋捕肩挑小販；

translations.literal: not to arrest peddlers carrying salt on shoulder-poles;
translations.idiomatic: they must not arrest petty peddlers carrying salt on shoulder-poles;

sentences.zh: 鹽場徵課不得刑比。

translations.literal: and that salt-field tax collection must not employ corporal punishment by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: and salt-field tax collection must not rely on corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「所奏各條皆是。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Each item you have memorialized is correct.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'Every point in your memorial is sound.'

sentences.zh: 汝先過刻，茲乃事事以寬沽名。

translations.literal: You were formerly too severe; now on every matter you use leniency to buy a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: You used to be excessively harsh; now you court popularity by leniency on every issue.'

sentences.zh: 過猶不及，汝其識之！

translations.literal: To go too far is as bad as not going far enough—mark this well!
translations.idiomatic: Excess is no better than deficiency—remember that!'

sentences.zh: 」尋請裁鹽場協辦鹽大使，改海寧草塘為石塘。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he requested the abolition of assistant salt commissioners at the salt fields and the conversion of Haining's sod seawall into a stone seawall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he asked to abolish assistant salt commissioners at the salt fields and to rebuild Haining's earthen seawall in stone.

sentences.zh: 既，又請濬備塘河運石。

translations.literal: Later he again requested dredging the backup seawall canal to transport stone.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to dredge the backup seawall canal to transport building stone.

sentences.zh: 五年，上諭曰：「盧焯至浙江，沽名邀譽，舉鄉賢名宦，絡繹不絕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor instructed: 'Since Lu Chao reached Zhejiang he has courted reputation and sought praise, recommending local worthies and famous officials without cease.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1740 the emperor said: 'Since Lu Chao arrived in Zhejiang he has been currying favor, nominating local worthies and celebrated officials in an endless stream.'

sentences.zh: 海塘外已漲沙數十里，焯既請停草塘歲修，又請改建石塘。

translations.literal: Outside the seawall sand had already accreted for several tens of li; Chao had both requested stopping annual sod-wall repairs and requested rebuilding as a stone seawall.
translations.idiomatic: Sand had already built up for dozens of li beyond the seawall, yet Chao first asked to halt annual repairs to the earthen dike and then asked to rebuild it in stone.

sentences.zh: 心無定見，惟事揣摩，已彰明較著矣。

translations.literal: His mind has no fixed view; he only guesses at what is wanted—this is already glaringly clear.
translations.idiomatic: He has no settled judgment and only tries to guess what I want—this is already perfectly obvious.'

sentences.zh: 」六年，左都御史劉吳龍劾焯營私受賄，上解焯任，命總督德沛、副都統旺扎爾按治，事皆實，請奪官刑訊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Left Censor-in-chief Liu Wulong impeached Chao for private dealings and taking bribes. The emperor relieved Chao of his post and ordered Governor-general Depè and Vice Banner Commander Wangzhar to investigate; the charges were all substantiated, and they requested deprivation of office and interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1741 Left Censor-in-chief Liu Wulong accused Chao of corruption and bribery. The emperor removed him from office and ordered Governor-general Depè and Vice Banner Commander Wangzhar to investigate; every charge was proved, and they recommended stripping his rank and putting him to the question.

sentences.zh: 事連嘉湖道呂守曾、嘉興知府楊景震。

translations.literal: The case implicated Jiahu Circuit intendant Lü Shouzeng and Jiaxing prefect Yang Jingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The case also involved Jiahu circuit intendant Lü Shouzeng and Jiaxing prefect Yang Jingzhen.

sentences.zh: 守曾已擢山西布政使，逮至浙江，自殺。

translations.literal: Shouzeng had already been promoted to treasurer of Shanxi; when arrested and brought to Zhejiang, he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzeng had already been promoted to Shanxi treasurer; when he was arrested and brought to Zhejiang, he committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 杭州民數百為焯訟冤，毀副都統廳前鼓亭。

translations.literal: Several hundred Hangzhou residents petitioned on Chao's behalf, claiming injustice, and destroyed the drum pavilion in front of the vice banner commander's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Hangzhou residents marched to plead Chao's innocence and tore down the drum pavilion before the vice banner commander's office.

sentences.zh: 德沛等以聞，上諭責辦理不妥。

translations.literal: Depè and the others reported this; the emperor instructed and rebuked them for improper handling.
translations.idiomatic: Depè reported the incident, and the emperor rebuked them for mishandling the case.

sentences.zh: 七年，讞上，焯、景震皆坐不枉法贓，擬絞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the verdict was submitted; Chao and Jingzhen were both convicted of taking bribes without perverting the law and were sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1742 the final judgment was handed up: Chao and Jingzhen were both found guilty of taking bribes without perverting justice and were sentenced to death by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 八年，焯以完贓減等，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because Chao made restitution of the illicit gains, his penalty was reduced by one degree and he was banished to military garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: In 1743, because he had made full restitution, his sentence was reduced and he was exiled to garrison labor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上南巡，閱海塘，念焯勞，召還。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, during the emperor's southern tour, he inspected the seawall and, recalling Chao's labors, summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: In 1751, on a southern tour, the emperor inspected the seawall, remembered Chao's service, and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授鴻臚寺少卿，署陝西西安巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and acted as governor of Xi'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 he was made vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and served as acting governor of Xi'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調署湖北，以陳宏謀代焯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to act in Hubei, with Chen Hongmou replacing Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1756 he was transferred to act as governor of Hubei, with Chen Hongmou slated to replace him.

sentences.zh: 宏謀未至，上命發歸化城米運金川饋軍，急驛諭宏謀。

translations.literal: Before Hongmou arrived, the emperor ordered grain from Guihua City sent to provision the army in Jinchuan, urgently dispatching a courier to instruct Hongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hongmou arrived, the throne ordered grain from Guihua City shipped to supply the Jinchuan campaign and sent an urgent courier to inform Hongmou.

sentences.zh: 焯發視，奏言：「歸化城雖產米，路遠費重；

translations.literal: Chao inspected and memorialized: 'Although Guihua City produces grain, the route is long and the cost heavy;
translations.idiomatic: Chao investigated and reported: 'Guihua City does produce grain, but the route is long and the cost prohibitive;

sentences.zh: 西安有貯米，先發以饋軍。

translations.literal: Xi'an has stored grain—issue it first to provision the army.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an has grain in store—let that be issued first to feed the troops.'

sentences.zh: 仍請擅行罪。

translations.literal: He still requested punishment for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He still asked to be punished for acting without authorization.'

sentences.zh: 」上嘉焯知大體，合機宜，實授湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Chao for grasping the larger situation and fitting the occasion, and formally appointed him governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Chao for understanding the larger situation and acting appropriately, and confirmed him as governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，西安布政使劉藻入覲，言焯在西安入貢方物，但量給薄值；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Xi'an treasurer Liu Zao came to court and said that in Xi'an Chao had accepted tribute goods but only paid scant prices;
translations.idiomatic: In 1757 Xi'an treasurer Liu Zao presented himself at court and reported that while in Xi'an Chao had accepted local tribute goods but paid only token prices;

sentences.zh: 及調任湖北，欲借庫帑，未應付。

translations.literal: and that after his transfer to Hubei he had wished to borrow from the treasury but had not been accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: and that after moving to Hubei he had tried to borrow from the provincial treasury but had been refused.

sentences.zh: 上責焯負恩，奪官，戍巴里坤。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Chao for ingratitude, stripped his office, and banished him to Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused Chao of betraying his favor, stripped his rank, and exiled him to Barkol.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，召還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1767.

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿，佟佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Tu Erbing'a, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbing'a, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授吏部筆帖式，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a clerk in the Board of Civil Appointments and was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Board of Civil Appointments and rose through successive promotions to director.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，授陝西甘肅道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed to the Shaanxi-Gansu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1738 he was appointed intendant of the Shaanxi-Gansu circuit.

sentences.zh: 累遷雲南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to treasurer of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was elevated to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1747 he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 十五年，永嘉知縣楊茂虧銀米，圖爾炳阿令後政彌補結案。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yongjia magistrate Yang Mao was short in silver and grain; Tu Erbing'a ordered his successor to make up the deficit and closed the case.
translations.idiomatic: In 1750 Yongjia magistrate Yang Mao was found short in silver and grain; Tu Erbing'a ordered his successor to make good the deficit and closed the case.

sentences.zh: 總督碩色論劾，上責圖爾炳阿欺隱徇庇，奪官，逮京師，下刑部治罪，坐監守自盜，擬斬監候。

translations.literal: Governor-general Shuose impeached him in a memorial; the emperor rebuked Tu Erbing'a for concealment and favoritism, stripped his office, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and handed him to the Board of Punishments, which convicted him of custodial theft and sentenced him to beheading after the autumn assizes.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Shuose memorialized against him; the emperor condemned Tu Erbing'a for covering up the case and showing favoritism, stripped his rank, had him brought to Beijing, and referred him to the Board of Punishments, which convicted him of custodial embezzlement and sentenced him to beheading, commuted after review.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上以圖爾炳阿贓未入己，釋出獄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor, because Tu Erbing'a's illicit gains had not entered his own pocket, released him from prison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1752 the emperor ruled that Tu Erbing'a had not personally profited from the shortfall and released him from prison.

sentences.zh: 授吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授河南布政使，調山東，又復還河南。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed treasurer of Henan, transferred to Shandong, and then returned again to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made treasurer of Henan, transferred to Shandong, and then sent back to Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was elevated to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上南巡，江蘇布政使夏邑彭家屏以病告家居，覲徐州行在，入對，言鄉縣被水。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, during the emperor's southern tour, Jiangsu treasurer Peng Jiaping of Xiayi, having reported illness and retired home, presented himself at the traveling palace in Xuzhou, was received in audience, and said his home county had suffered flooding.
translations.idiomatic: In 1757, on the emperor's southern tour, Jiangsu treasurer Peng Jiaping of Xiayi, who had retired on grounds of illness, came to the traveling palace at Xuzhou, was granted an audience, and reported flooding in his home district.

sentences.zh: 上諮圖爾炳阿，圖爾炳阿奏收成至九分，上責圖爾炳阿文過。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted Tu Erbing'a; Tu Erbing'a memorialized that the harvest reached nine-tenths, and the emperor rebuked him for glossing over faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Tu Erbing'a, who reported a harvest of ninety percent; the emperor rebuked him for whitewashing the situation.

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿又奏「去歲被水尚未成災」，上斥為怙惡不悛。

translations.literal: Tu Erbing'a again memorialized that 'last year's flooding has not yet become a disaster,' and the emperor denounced him as persisting in evil without repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbing'a then reported that 'last year's floods have not yet amounted to a disaster,' and the emperor denounced him as incorrigible.

sentences.zh: 遣員外郎觀音保密察災狀得實，上奪圖爾炳阿官，髮烏里雅蘇台效力。

translations.literal: He dispatched Vice Director Guanyinbao to investigate secretly; the disaster conditions were found true. The emperor stripped Tu Erbing'a of office and sent him to serve at Uliastai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Vice Director Guanyinbao to investigate in secret and confirmed the disaster. The emperor stripped Tu Erbing'a of his rank and sent him to serve at Uliastai.

sentences.zh: 上發徐州，夏邑民張欽、劉元德詣行在訴知縣孫默諱災及治賑不實，上親鞫，元德言諸生段昌緒指使。

translations.literal: As the emperor departed Xuzhou, Xiayi commoners Zhang Qin and Liu Yuande came to the traveling palace to accuse Magistrate Sun Mo of concealing the disaster and mishandling relief; the emperor personally examined them, and Yuande said the licentiate Duan Changxu had instigated them.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor left Xuzhou, Xiayi residents Zhang Qin and Liu Yuande came to the traveling palace to accuse Magistrate Sun Mo of concealing the disaster and bungling relief. The emperor questioned them personally, and Yuande said the student Duan Changxu had put them up to it.

sentences.zh: 上復遣侍衛成林會圖爾炳阿至夏邑按治，於昌緒家得傳鈔吳三桂檄。

translations.literal: The emperor again dispatched Bodyguard Cheng Lin to join Tu Erbing'a in going to Xiayi to investigate; at Changxu's home they found circulated copies of a proclamation of Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Bodyguard Cheng Lin with Tu Erbing'a to investigate in Xiayi, where they found copied proclamations of Wu Sangui in Changxu's house.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「圖爾炳阿察出逆檄，緝邪之功大，諱災之罪小。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Tu Erbing'a uncovered the treasonous proclamation—his merit in suppressing heterodoxy is great, his offense in concealing the disaster is small.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Tu Erbing'a uncovered the seditious proclamation; his merit in rooting out sedition is great, and his offense in concealing the disaster is small.'

sentences.zh: 且以如此梗不知化之民，而治其司牧者以罪，是不益長澆風乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, for such stubborn and unregenerate commoners, to punish their local officials—would this not only encourage a degenerate trend?
translations.idiomatic: And for subjects this stubborn and unreformed, to punish their magistrates instead—would that not only encourage moral decay?'

sentences.zh: 免圖爾炳阿罪，仍留巡撫任治賑。

translations.literal: Tu Erbing'a's punishment was remitted and he was retained in the governorship to manage relief.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbing'a was pardoned and kept in office as governor to oversee relief.

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿若因有前此罪斥之旨，心存成見，或不釋然於災民，則是自取罪戾，亦不能逃朕洞鑑。

translations.literal: If Tu Erbing'a, because of the earlier edict rebuking him, harbors prejudice or is not reconciled to the disaster victims, then he brings punishment on himself and cannot escape My penetrating scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: If Tu Erbing'a, remembering my earlier rebuke, holds a grudge or takes out his resentment on the flood victims, he will bring punishment on himself—and he cannot escape my scrutiny.'

sentences.zh: 」尋家屏亦以藏禁書罪至死，圖爾炳阿仍以匿災下吏議，奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jiaping was also sentenced to death for concealing banned books; Tu Erbing'a was still referred to the judicial authorities for concealing the disaster, stripped of office, but ordered to remain in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jiaping was also sentenced to death for hiding banned books; Tu Erbing'a was again referred to the courts for concealing the disaster, stripped of rank, but ordered to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，召詣京師，命往烏里雅蘇台治餉。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned to the capital and ordered to go to Uliastai to manage provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was summoned to Beijing and sent to Uliastai to manage supplies.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授貴州巡撫，二十九年，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed governor of Guizhou; in the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1763 he was appointed governor of Guizhou; in 1764 he was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，病作，遣醫往視。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he fell ill; the emperor sent a physician to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1765 he fell ill, and the throne sent a physician to see him.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 阿思哈，薩克達氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Asiha, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Asiha, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 自官學生考授內閣中書，累遷刑部郎中，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: From student of the Imperial Academy he passed examination for appointment as secretary in the Grand Secretariat, was promoted repeatedly to director in the Board of Punishments, and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the examination from the Imperial Academy, he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, rose through the Board of Punishments to director, and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，擢甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he was elevated to treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1745 he was promoted to provincial treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was elevated to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1749 he was made governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「各營操演槍砲，須實子彈。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'When each garrison drills with muskets and cannon, live ammunition is required.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'When garrisons drill with muskets and cannon, they must use live ammunition.'

sentences.zh: 營馬應令騎兵自飼。

translations.literal: Garrison horses should be ordered to be fed by the cavalry themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison horses should be fed by the cavalrymen themselves.'

sentences.zh: 技藝以純熟得用為要，步法、架勢不必朝更夕改。

translations.literal: In martial skill what matters is pure mastery that can be put to use; footwork and postures need not be changed morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Combat skill should be judged by practical mastery, not by constantly changing footwork and forms from day to day.'

sentences.zh: 」上嘉其言得要。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words as hitting the essential point.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his advice as sound.

sentences.zh: 旋調山西。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 十六年，平陽旱，未親往撫卹，詔責之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Pingyang suffered drought; he did not go in person to comfort and relieve, and an edict rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1751 Pingyang suffered drought, but he did not go in person to comfort the people, and an imperial edict rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，蒲、解等處复災，請以平陽富民捐款解河東道加賑。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Pu, Xie, and other places again suffered disaster; he requested that wealthy households in Pingyang donate funds to be remitted to the Hedong Circuit for supplemental relief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1752 Pu, Xie, and other districts were hit again; he asked wealthy households in Pingyang to donate funds to the Hedong circuit for supplemental relief.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「賑濟蠲緩，重者數百萬，少亦數十萬，悉動正帑，從無顧惜。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: 'For relief, tax remission, and deferment, the heavy cases run to several millions and the light to several hundreds of thousands—all drawn from the regular treasury without stint.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: 'Relief, tax remission, and deferments cost millions in the worst cases and hundreds of thousands in the least—all paid from the regular treasury without hesitation.'

sentences.zh: 富戶所捐幾何，貯庫助賑，殊非體制。

translations.literal: How much can wealthy households donate? To store it in the treasury to aid relief is quite contrary to proper practice.
translations.idiomatic: What can wealthy donors really contribute? Storing private donations in the treasury for relief is entirely improper.'

sentences.zh: 此端一開，則偏災之地，貧民既苦艱食，富戶又令出貲。

translations.literal: Once this precedent is opened, in locally stricken areas the poor already suffer from scarce food and the wealthy are again ordered to pay out funds.
translations.idiomatic: Once that door is opened, in every partial disaster the poor already go hungry while the rich are pressed for money too.'

sentences.zh: 國家撫卹災黎，何忍出此？

translations.literal: When the state comforts and relieves disaster victims, how can we bear to resort to this?
translations.idiomatic: When the state relieves disaster victims, how can we stoop to such a scheme?'

sentences.zh: 」責阿思哈卑鄙錯謬，不勝巡撫任，召還，奪官。

translations.literal: He rebuked Asiha as base and mistaken, unfit for the governorship, recalled him, and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: He condemned Asiha as mean and misguided, unfit to serve as governor, recalled him, and stripped his rank.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命以布政使銜往準噶爾軍前經理糧運。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered, with the rank of provincial treasurer, to go to the Zunghar front to manage grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 he was sent to the Zunghar front with treasurer's rank to manage grain supply.

sentences.zh: 擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命署江西巡撫，蒞任，清理屯田，尋真除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to act as governor of Jiangxi; on assuming office he cleared up garrison fields, and shortly afterward received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1757 he was appointed acting governor of Jiangxi; on taking office he sorted out garrison land tenure and was soon confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 學政謝溶生劾阿思哈婪賄派累，命尚書劉統勳、侍郎常鈞等按鞫，得實，擬絞。

translations.literal: The provincial education commissioner Xie Rongsheng impeached Asiha for greedily accepting bribes and imposing burdensome levies; the emperor ordered Ministers Liu Tongxun and Vice Minister Chang Jun and others to investigate and try the case; the charges were found true, and strangulation was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial education commissioner Xie Rongsheng impeached Asiha for extortion and corrupt levies. The emperor ordered Minister Liu Tongxun, Vice Minister Chang Jun, and others to investigate; the charges proved true and strangulation was recommended.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，詔免罪，以三品頂戴髮烏魯木齊效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year an edict pardoned his crime; with third-rank hat insignia he was dispatched to Urumqi to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he was pardoned by edict and sent to serve at Urumqi with third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，命往伊犁協同辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was ordered to go to Ili to assist in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1763 he was assigned to Ili to assist in local administration.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授廣東巡撫，調河南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed governor of Guangdong, then transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1764 he was made governor of Guangdong, then transferred to Henan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，疏言：「衛河運道淺阻，濬縣三官廟、老鸛嘴諸地砂礓挺據河心，重載尤艱浮送。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he memorialized: 'The Wei River transport channel is shallow and obstructed; at Sanguan Temple in Jun County, Old Stork Beak, and other places hardpan juts into the river's center, making it especially difficult to float heavily laden cargo downstream.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1765 he memorialized: 'The Wei River shipping route runs shallow and obstructed. At Sanguan Temple and Old Stork Beak in Jun County and elsewhere, hardpan ridges stand in mid-channel, making downstream transport of heavily laden boats especially arduous.'

sentences.zh: 向於上、下游淺處建築草壩以束水勢。

translations.literal: Previously, at shallow points up- and downstream, grass dams had been built to confine the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: Grass dams had previously been built at shallow stretches upstream and downstream to concentrate the current.'

sentences.zh: 詳考河形，夏秋水盛，無須草壩；

translations.literal: On close examination of the river's form, in summer and autumn when water is abundant grass dams are unnecessary;
translations.idiomatic: A careful survey showed that in summer and autumn, when water is plentiful, grass dams serve no purpose;'

sentences.zh: 冬令源澀，草壩亦屬無益。

translations.literal: in winter when sources run sluggish, grass dams likewise afford no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: in winter, when the headwaters run low, they are useless as well.'

sentences.zh: 不如於上游先期蓄水，臨時開放。

translations.literal: It would be better to store water upstream in advance and release it when needed.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to impound water upstream in advance and release it as needed.'

sentences.zh: 飭府縣督河員於九月望後起，至漕船出境止，暫閉外河以上民渠，使水歸官渠，重運自可疏通。

translations.literal: He directed prefecture and county officials and river commissioners to begin after the mid-ninth month and continue until grain transports leave the jurisdiction; temporarily closing civilian canals above the outer river so water flows into official channels, heavy transport can then be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered prefectural, county, and river officials to begin after the fifteenth day of the ninth month and continue until the grain fleet had passed, temporarily closing private canals above the outer river so water would enter the official channel—enough to ease heavily laden shipping.'

sentences.zh: 鑿去砂礓，並集夫疏濬浮沙，以利漕運。

translations.literal: Hardpan should be cut away, and laborers assembled to dredge floating sand, to benefit grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Hardpan should be removed and labor mobilized to dredge silt, easing grain transport.'

sentences.zh: 」又請借司庫閒款，委員分購河工料物，以除沿河州縣按畝派累，均報聞。

translations.literal: He also requested borrowing idle funds from the provincial treasury, with commissioners dispatched to purchase river-work materials in batches, so as to eliminate levies per mu imposed on counties along the river—all reported and approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to borrow idle provincial funds and send agents to buy river materials in bulk, eliminating per-mu levies on counties along the route. Both proposals were approved.'

sentences.zh: 三十四年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1769 he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 師徵緬甸，阿思哈出銅壁關至蠻暮軍中，奏軍中糧馬不敷。

translations.literal: When the army marched against Burma, Asiha went from Tongbi Pass to the army at Manmu and memorialized that army grain and horses were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign Asiha went from Tongbi Pass to the army at Manmu and reported shortages of grain and horses.

sentences.zh: 上責其畏難，解任，以副都統銜在領隊大臣上行走。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for fearing hardship; he was dismissed from office and, with the rank of assistant commandant, was ordered to serve under the expedition commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of shrinking from hardship, removed him from office, and assigned him to serve under the expedition commander with assistant commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 旋召為吏部侍郎，入對失上指，奪官，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned as vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments; in audience he missed the emperor's intent; his office was stripped and he was exiled to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, but in audience he displeased the emperor, was stripped of rank, and exiled to Ili.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，釋回，仍充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was released and returned, again serving as a grand council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 he was released and restored as a grand council clerk.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 大學士舒赫德師討王倫，命阿思哈偕額駙拉旺多爾濟率健銳、火器兩營以往。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Suhede led troops to suppress Wang Lun; Asiha was ordered to accompany Imperial Son-in-Law Lawang Duo'erji leading the Elite and Firearms brigades.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Suhede marched against Wang Lun, Asiha was ordered to accompany Imperial Son-in-Law Lawang Duo'erji at the head of the Elite and Firearms brigades.

sentences.zh: 事定，拉旺多爾濟言城北搜剿王倫餘黨，阿思哈未同往，下吏議，奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: When matters were settled, Lawang Duo'erji reported that in searching north of the city for Wang Lun's remaining followers Asiha had not gone along; the case was referred to officials for deliberation, his office was stripped, but he was ordered to remain in his post.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, Lawang Duo'erji reported that Asiha had not joined a search north of the city for Wang Lun's remaining followers. Officials were ordered to investigate; he was stripped of rank but allowed to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，署吏部尚書，旋授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he acted as minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, then was appointed grain transport governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1776 he served as acting minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, then was appointed grain transport governor-general.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡莊恪。

translations.literal: He died; imperial sacrifices and burial honors were granted, and he was posthumously titled Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted state funeral honors; his posthumous title was Zhuangke ('Steadfast and Reverent').

sentences.zh: 阿思哈初撫江西，上眷之獨厚。

translations.literal: When Asiha first served as governor of Jiangxi, the emperor favored him with special warmth.
translations.idiomatic: When Asiha first governed Jiangxi, the emperor favored him unusually.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫衛哲治入覲，上問各省督撫孰為最劣，哲治引罪，上謂：「姑置汝！

translations.literal: Guangxi governor Wei Zhezhi came to audience; the emperor asked which governor or governor-general in the provinces was worst; Zhezhi pleaded guilty; the emperor said: 'Leave you aside for now!'
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi governor Wei Zhezhi came to court, the emperor asked who among the provincial governors was the worst. Zhezhi took the blame himself. The emperor said: 'Never mind you for now—'

sentences.zh: 」哲治舉阿思哈對，時以為難能。

translations.literal: Zhezhi named Asiha in reply; at the time this was regarded as a difficult feat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhi named Asiha instead. At the time many considered that a remarkable act of candor.'

sentences.zh: 宮兆麟，字伯厚，江南懷遠人。

translations.literal: Gong Zhaolin, courtesy name Bohou, was a native of Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhaolin, styled Bohou, was from Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 自貢生授湖北安陸通判，累遷至山東糧道。

translations.literal: From presented scholar he was appointed Anlu subprefect in Hubei, and through successive promotions reached grain intendant of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a presented scholar appointed Anlu subprefect in Hubei, he rose through successive posts to grain intendant of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年，授湖南按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he was appointed provincial judge of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1766 he was appointed provincial judge of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 桂陽州民侯七郎毆殺從兄岳添，賄其兄學添自承。

translations.literal: A commoner of Guiyang Prefecture, Hou Qilang, beat to death his cousin Yue Tian; he bribed his elder brother Xue Tian to confess in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Qilang, a commoner of Guiyang Prefecture, beat his cousin Yue Tian to death and bribed his elder brother Xue Tian to confess on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 知州張宏燧讞上，巡撫李因培疑之，令兆麟詳鞫得實。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Hongsui submitted the verdict upward; Governor Li Yinpei was suspicious and ordered Zhaolin to examine and try the case in detail; the truth was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Hongsui sent up the verdict, but Governor Li Yinpei was suspicious and had Zhaolin conduct a detailed trial; the facts came out.

sentences.zh: 因培調福建去，巡撫常鈞庇宏燧，以七郎呼冤劾兆麟，兆麟亦入奏。

translations.literal: When Yinpei was transferred to Fujian, Governor Chang Jun shielded Hongsui; Qilang cried injustice and impeached Zhaolin, and Zhaolin also memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Yinpei was transferred to Fujian, Governor Chang Jun protected Hongsui. Qilang cried injustice and impeached Zhaolin, who memorialized in turn.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎期成額會總督定長按治，如兆麟讞；

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Qicheng'e to join Governor-General Ding Chang in investigating and handling the case according to Zhaolin's verdict;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Qicheng'e with Governor-General Ding Chang to investigate; the case followed Zhaolin's findings;'

sentences.zh: 兆麟又發宏燧買金行賄狀，期成額等奏聞，逮訊，買金非行賄，乃迎合因培及湖北布政使赫升額意指，代武陵知縣馮其柘補虧空。

translations.literal: Zhaolin further exposed Hongsui's act of purchasing gold to bribe; Qicheng'e and others memorialized; on arrest and interrogation, the gold purchase was not bribery but rather complied with Yinpei and Hubei provincial treasurer Hesheng'e's wishes to cover Wuling magistrate Feng Qizhe's deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin also uncovered Hongsui's gold purchases. After Qicheng'e reported this and arrests were made, it emerged that the gold was not a bribe but had been bought to oblige Yinpei and Hubei treasurer Hesheng'e and to make up a deficit for Wuling magistrate Feng Qizhe.'

sentences.zh: 因培、赫升額、常鈞、宏燧皆坐譴。

translations.literal: Yinpei, Hesheng'e, Chang Jun, and Hongsui were all punished for their involvement.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpei, Hesheng'e, Chang Jun, and Hongsui were all punished.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，兆麟調雲南按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Zhaolin was transferred to provincial judge of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1767 Zhaolin was transferred to provincial judge of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷布政使，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was moved to provincial treasurer and promoted governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1768 he became provincial treasurer and was promoted governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 雲南軍營需硝，敕兆麟籌畫，兆麟以廣西舊存硝七萬七千餘斤運剝隘，复撥通省營貯火藥二十萬斤繼運，得旨嘉許。

translations.literal: Yunnan's military camps needed saltpeter; an edict ordered Zhaolin to plan supplies; Zhaolin shipped more than seventy-seven thousand jin of saltpeter previously stored in Guangxi to Bo'ai, then allocated two hundred thousand jin of gunpowder stored in camps province-wide for continued transport; an approving edict was received.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan's military camps needed saltpeter, the emperor ordered Zhaolin to arrange supply. He shipped over 77,000 jin of saltpeter stored in Guangxi to Bo'ai, then forwarded 200,000 jin of gunpowder from Guangxi arsenals. The emperor praised the effort.

sentences.zh: 調湖南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，又調貴州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was again transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1770 he was transferred again, to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 桐梓縣民為亂，命速赴任，會湖廣總督吳達善捕治。

translations.literal: Commoners of Tongzi County rose in disorder; he was ordered to hurry to his post and join Huguang Governor-General Wu Dashan in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners in Tongzi County rebelled, he was ordered to take post quickly and join Huguang governor-general Wu Dashan in suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 亂定，古州黨堆寨苗香要等為亂，复偕吳達善督兵捕誅之。

translations.literal: When the disorder was settled, the Miao Xiangyao and others of Dangdui Stockade in Guzhou again rebelled; he again joined Wu Dashan in commanding troops to capture and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: After that rebellion was crushed, the Miao leader Xiangyao and others at Dangdui Stockade in Guzhou rose again; Zhaolin again joined Wu Dashan in leading troops to capture and execute them.

sentences.zh: 兆麟奏黨堆寨苗老呴以阻香要亂被殺，令即寨立廟以祀良苗，並將死義被旌及香要叛逆伏誅狀，譯苗語榜廟門，俾令警戒；

translations.literal: Zhaolin memorialized that the Miao elder Xu of Dangdui Stockade had been killed for blocking Xiangyao's rebellion; he ordered a temple built at the stockade to honor loyal Miao, and had the deeds of those who died loyally and were honored, and of Xiangyao's rebellion and execution, translated into Miao and posted at the temple gate for warning;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin reported that Elder Xu of Dangdui Stockade had been killed for opposing Xiangyao's revolt. He had a temple built at the stockade to honor loyal Miao and posted notices in Miao at its gate describing those honored for dying in loyalty and Xiangyao's rebellion and execution, as a warning;'

sentences.zh: 並請移駐將吏，建下江營土城，駐兵鎮撫。

translations.literal: He also requested relocating stationed officers, building an earthen fort at Xiajiang Camp, and stationing troops to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to redeploy officers, build an earthen fort at Xiajiang Camp, and garrison troops to keep order.'

sentences.zh: 是夏，兆麟奏請於鄰省湖南、四川、廣西買米運貴州糶濟。

translations.literal: That summer Zhaolin memorialized requesting to purchase grain in neighboring provinces Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangxi and transport it to Guizhou for sale as relief.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Zhaolin asked permission to buy grain in Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangxi and ship it to Guizhou for relief sales.

sentences.zh: 至秋，豐收，復奏請停運。

translations.literal: By autumn the harvest was abundant, and he again memorialized requesting that transport be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn the harvest was good and he asked to halt the shipments.

sentences.zh: 上斥其冒昧，勗令詳慎。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked his rashness and urged him to be thorough and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked his impulsiveness and urged greater care.

sentences.zh: 兆麟復奏請簡發知府三員赴貴州，上以「此端一開，各省效尤，妨吏部選法；

translations.literal: Zhaolin again memorialized requesting that three prefects be specially dispatched to Guizhou; the emperor said: 'Once this precedent is opened, every province will follow suit and obstruct the Board's appointment methods;'
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin then asked that three prefects be specially sent to Guizhou. The emperor warned: 'Open that door and every province will follow, undermining the Board's appointment system;'

sentences.zh: 且開幸進之門」，下旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: moreover it opens a gate to lucky advancement,' and issued a stern edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: and it opens a path for favor-seekers.' A stern edict followed.'

sentences.zh: 會貴州布政使觀音保入覲，訐兆麟粗率喜自誇，口給便捷，人號為「鐵嘴」。

translations.literal: When Guizhou provincial treasurer Guanyinbao came to audience, he denounced Zhaolin as crude, reckless, and fond of boasting; quick with speech, he was called 'Iron Mouth.'
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou treasurer Guanyinbao came to court, he accused Zhaolin of being brash and boastful, quick-tongued and glib; people called him 'Iron Mouth.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「觀音保人已粗率，今尚以兆麟為粗率，則粗率更甚可知。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Guanyinbao is already crude and reckless; if he still finds Zhaolin crude and reckless, then Zhaolin must be cruder still, as one can infer.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Guanyinbao is already a rough man; if even he finds Zhaolin crude, Zhaolin must be rougher still.'

sentences.zh: 」諭兆麟猛省痛改。

translations.literal: Zhaolin was instructed to reflect deeply and reform thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin was told to take the warning to heart and mend his ways.'

sentences.zh: 尋詔詣京師，降補甘肅按察使。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict summoned him to the capital and he was demoted to provincial judge of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the capital and demoted to provincial judge of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，坐貴州任內失察廠員虧欠鉛斤，奪官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, for failure to detect during his Guizhou tenure that factory staff were deficient in lead owed, his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1771 he was stripped of rank for failing during his Guizhou tenure to detect lead shortages among factory clerks.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，東巡，兆麟迎駕，詔與三品銜。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, during the eastern tour, Zhaolin met the imperial procession and was granted third-rank insignia by edict.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's 1776 eastern tour, Zhaolin met the procession and was granted third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1781.

sentences.zh: 楊景素，字樸園，江南甘泉人，提督捷孫。

translations.literal: Yang Jingsu, courtesy name Puyuan, was a native of Ganquan in Jiangnan, grandson of Grand Coordinator Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingsu, styled Puyuan, was from Ganquan in Jiangnan and grandson of Grand Coordinator Jie.

sentences.zh: 父鑄，古北口總兵。

translations.literal: His father Zhu was commander at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhu was garrison commander at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 景素孱弱，不好章句，貧不能自給。

translations.literal: Jingsu was frail and weak, disliked textual study, and in poverty could not support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu was sickly, had no taste for classical scholarship, and was too poor to support himself.

sentences.zh: 入貲授縣丞，發直隸河工效力。

translations.literal: He entered office by purchase of rank as county assistant magistrate and was sent to serve on Zhili river works.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way into office as a county assistant magistrate and was assigned to Zhili river works.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，補蠡縣縣丞，累遷保定知府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed county assistant magistrate of Li County, and through successive promotions reached prefect of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In 1738 he became assistant magistrate of Li County and rose through successive posts to prefect of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授福建汀漳龍道。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1753 he was appointed intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 漳浦民蔡榮祖欲為亂，景素率營卒擒斬之。

translations.literal: A commoner of Zhangpu, Cai Rongzu, intended to rebel; Jingsu led camp soldiers to capture and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangpu commoner Cai Rongzu plotted rebellion, Jingsu led garrison troops to capture and execute him.

sentences.zh: 調台灣道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit.

sentences.zh: 釐定漢民墾種地，並生熟番界址。

translations.literal: He fixed boundaries of Han reclaimed land and of raw and acculturated aboriginal territories.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the boundaries of Han settlers' reclaimed land and the frontier between raw and acculturated aboriginal peoples.

sentences.zh: 革遊民為通譯而不法者，代以熟番。

translations.literal: He eliminated indigent Han who served as interpreters but acted lawlessly, replacing them with acculturated aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: He removed lawless Han vagrants who worked as interpreters and replaced them with acculturated aborigines.

sentences.zh: 又禁入山採木，借修造戰船材料為名，累諸番。

translations.literal: He also forbade entering the mountains to cut timber under the pretext of gathering materials to repair and build war vessels, which had burdened the aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: He also banned timber gathering in the hills under the pretext of supplying warship repairs, a burden long imposed on the aborigines.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授河南按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed provincial judge of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1768 he was appointed provincial judge of Henan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，擢甘肅布政使，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was promoted provincial treasurer of Gansu and transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1770 he became treasurer of Gansu and was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 命從尚書裘曰修勘察堤埝各工。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Minister Qiu Yixiu in inspecting dikes and embankment works.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to accompany Minister Qiu Yixiu on inspections of dikes and embankments.

sentences.zh: 坐失察雄縣知縣胡錫瑛侵蝕災賑，下吏議，奪官，命留任，俟八年無過，方准開復。

translations.literal: For failure to detect Xiong County magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, the case was referred to officials; his office was stripped but he was ordered to remain in post, and only after eight years without fault would restoration be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank for failing to detect Xiong County magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, but allowed to remain in office; restoration would come only after eight years without fault.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂，大學士舒赫德督兵討之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year commoners of Shouzhang, Wang Lun, rebelled; Grand Secretary Suhede commanded troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 Wang Lun led a rebellion in Shouzhang; Grand Secretary Suhede took command against him.

sentences.zh: 上命景素具車馬濟師，令分守河西。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jingsu to provide carts and horses to aid the army and commanded him to hold the west bank of the river separately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jingsu to supply transport for the army and hold the west bank of the river.

sentences.zh: 賊以糧艘結浮橋欲渡，景素與總兵萬朝興、副將瑪爾當阿等督兵御之，董勸回民助師。

translations.literal: The rebels joined grain boats into a pontoon bridge to cross; Jingsu with Brigadier Wan Chaoxing, Deputy Commander Ma'erdang'a, and others commanded troops to resist, and urged Hui people to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lashed grain boats into a pontoon to cross the river. Jingsu, Brigadier Wan Chaoxing, Deputy Commander Ma'erdang'a, and others held them off and rallied local Muslims to support the army.

sentences.zh: 夜焚橋，賊不得渡。

translations.literal: At night they burned the bridge, and the rebels could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the bridge by night and kept the rebels from crossing.

sentences.zh: 事旋定，擢山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Matters were soon settled, and he was promoted governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was promoted governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 疏請編查保甲。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting compilation and inspection of baojia household registers.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to compile and inspect baojia registers.

sentences.zh: 四十年，疏請選京師健銳、火器營裨佐發山東，司營伍教演。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized requesting selection of adjutants from the capital's Elite and Firearms brigades to be sent to Shandong to manage camp drill and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he asked that adjutants from the capital's Elite and Firearms brigades be sent to Shandong to train local garrisons.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上東巡，臨視臨清毀橋斷道及亂民竄據所在，景素述當時戰狀，上嘉其勞，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, during the emperor's eastern tour, he personally viewed the destroyed bridges and severed roads at Linqing and where rebels had lurked; Jingsu narrated the fighting at the time; the emperor praised his labors and granted a yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: During the 1776 eastern tour the emperor inspected Linqing, where bridges had been destroyed and rebels had held ground. Jingsu described the fighting; the emperor praised his service and granted him a yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 汶上宋家窪舊渠淤墊，瀦水淹民田。

translations.literal: At Songjiawa in Wenshang the old canal was silted and choked, and pooled water flooded commoners' fields.
translations.idiomatic: The old canal at Songjiawa in Wenshang had silted up and standing water was flooding farmland.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，景素奏請濬舊渠，並開支河二，令仍趨南陽、昭陽二湖，下部議行。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year Jingsu memorialized requesting dredging of the old canal and opening two branch channels so water would again flow toward Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes; the memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1777 he asked to dredge the old canal and cut two branch channels to restore flow to Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes. The ministries approved.

sentences.zh: 擢兩廣總督，四十三年，調閩浙。

translations.literal: He was promoted governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; in the forty-third year he was transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi, then in 1778 transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「浙西歉收，總督楊廷璋請撥台灣倉穀十萬接濟。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Western Zhejiang suffered poor harvest; Governor-General Yang Tingzhang requested allocation of one hundred thousand shi of Taiwan granary grain for relief.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'Western Zhejiang had a poor harvest. Governor-General Yang Tingzhang asked to draw 100,000 shi of grain from Taiwan's granaries for relief.'

sentences.zh: 北風盛發，未能即到。

translations.literal: North winds were strong and the grain could not arrive immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Strong north winds would delay shipment.'

sentences.zh: 請於福州、福寧、興化、泉州四府屬撥倉穀十萬，聽商運赴嘉、湖出糶；

translations.literal: He requested that one hundred thousand shi of granary grain be drawn from the four prefectures of Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou, allowing merchants to transport it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for sale as relief;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed releasing 100,000 shi from granaries in Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou and letting merchants haul it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for relief sales;'

sentences.zh: 仍飭台灣運歸四府補倉。

translations.literal: Taiwan grain was still to be ordered transported back to replenish the four prefectures' granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan's granaries would later be restocked to replace the four prefectures' reserves.'

sentences.zh: 」得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: An approving edict was received with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and commended the plan.'

sentences.zh: 四十四年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 薦於易簡為布政使，上以易簡為大學士敏中弟，責景素。

translations.literal: He recommended Yu Yijian for provincial treasurer; the emperor, since Yijian was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong, rebuked Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Yu Yijian as treasurer, but the emperor rebuked him because Yijian was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒，贈太子太保，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bereavement grants were awarded according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month and was posthumously named Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the usual mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，兩廣總督巴延三奏景素操守不謹，並發官兵得贓縱盜狀。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year Guangdong-Guangxi Governor-General Bayansan memorialized that Jingsu's conduct had not been scrupulous and also exposed soldiers' acceptance of bribes and release of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1780 Governor-General Bayansan reported that Jingsu had been lax in integrity and that his troops had taken bribes and released bandits.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督薩載勘有河堤城垣工程，罰景素家屬承修。

translations.literal: Jiangnan-Jiangxi Governor-General Sazai investigated and found river-dike and city-wall projects owed; Jingsu's family was fined to undertake the repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan governor-general Sazai found unpaid river and city-wall works and ordered Jingsu's family to complete them as a penalty.

sentences.zh: 福康安又奏景素在兩廣婪索商捐六萬餘，責景素子炤限年繳還。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan further memorialized that Jingsu in Guangdong-Guangxi had greedily extorted more than sixty thousand in merchant levies; Jingsu's son Zhao was ordered to repay within a set term.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan also reported that Jingsu had extorted over 60,000 in merchant levies in Guangdong and Guangxi; his son Zhao was ordered to repay within a fixed term.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，以福建吏治廢弛，追咎景素，戍召伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, citing the slackening of Fujian official discipline, Jingsu was held accountable retroactively and exiled to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1789, blaming slack Fujian governance on him, Jingsu was punished retroactively and exiled to Ili.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，釋回。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794 he was released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 閔鶚元，字少儀，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Min Eyuan, courtesy name Shaoyi, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Min Eyuan, styled Shaoyi, was from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the tenth year of Qianlong, he was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1745 and was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中，督山東學政。

translations.literal: After a further promotion to director, he supervised as Shandong provincial education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director and appointed Shandong provincial education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，自學政授山東按察使，調安徽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, from education commissioner he was appointed provincial judge of Shandong, then transferred to Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1762 he moved from education commissioner to provincial judge of Shandong, then transferred to Anhui.

sentences.zh: 遷湖北布政使，調廣西、江寧。

translations.literal: He was promoted provincial treasurer of Hubei, transferred to Guangxi and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He became treasurer of Hubei and served successively in Guangxi and Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，遷安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was transferred to governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1776 he was transferred to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，雲貴總督李侍堯以贓敗，罪至斬，下大學士、九卿議，請從重立決；

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Li Shiyao was ruined by bribery; the offense warranted decapitation. The case was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers for deliberation, who requested immediate execution with aggravated severity;
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Li Shiyao was convicted of corruption, a capital offense. The case went to the grand secretaries and Nine Ministers, who recommended immediate execution;

sentences.zh: 復下各省督撫議，咸請如大學士九卿議。

translations.literal: It was again referred to the governors-general and governors of each province for deliberation; all requested conformity with the grand secretaries' and Nine Ministers' recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The case was then sent to every provincial governor for comment; all endorsed the capital recommendation.

sentences.zh: 鶚元窺上指欲寬侍堯，獨奏言：「侍堯歷任封疆，勤幹有為，中外推服。

translations.literal: Eyuan divined that the emperor wished to be lenient toward Shiyao and alone memorialized: 'Shiyao has served on the frontiers, diligent and capable, admired within and without.'
translations.idiomatic: Eyuan sensed that the emperor wished to spare Shiyao and alone memorialized: 'Shiyao has served on the frontiers with diligence and ability, and is respected throughout the bureaucracy.'

sentences.zh: 請用議勤、議能例，稍寬一線。

translations.literal: He requested application of the precedents for deliberating on diligence and on ability, with a slight margin of leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the precedents for rewarding diligence and ability be applied to grant him a measure of clemency.'

sentences.zh: 」上從之，侍堯得復起。

translations.literal: The emperor assented, and Shiyao was able to rise again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Shiyao was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1780 he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，甘肅布政使王亶望坐偽災冒賑得罪，事連鶚元弟同知鵷元。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year Gansu Provincial Treasurer Wang Tanwang was convicted for fabricating disaster and fraudulently claiming relief; the case implicated Eyuan's younger brother, sub-prefect Yuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1781 Gansu treasurer Wang Tanwang was convicted of inventing a disaster to claim relief funds; the case also implicated Eyuan's younger brother, sub-prefect Yuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 上責鶚元隱忍瞻徇，知其事而不舉，降三品頂戴，停廉俸。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for concealment and favoritism, knowing of the matter yet not reporting it; his insignia was reduced to third rank and his integrity stipend suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for covering up the affair and showing favoritism—he had known but not reported it. His rank insignia was reduced to third grade and his integrity stipend suspended.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，還原品頂戴，支廉俸如故。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year his original rank insignia was restored and his integrity stipend paid as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1783 his original rank insignia and integrity stipend were restored.

sentences.zh: 五十年，江南旱。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year Jiangnan suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: In 1785 Jiangnan suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 五月，鶚元奏淮、徐、海三府如得雨二三寸，猶可種雜糧。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Eyuan memorialized that in the three prefectures of Huai, Xu, and Hai, if two or three inches of rain fell, miscellaneous grains could still be planted.
translations.idiomatic: In May Eyuan reported that in the Huai, Xu, and Hai prefectures, if two or three inches of rain fell, farmers might still plant secondary crops.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「得雨二三寸未為霑足，焉能種雜糧？

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Two or three inches of rain is not sufficient soaking—how can miscellaneous grains be planted?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'Two or three inches of rain is not enough to soak the fields—how can anyone plant secondary crops?'

sentences.zh: 地方雨水，民瘼攸關。

translations.literal: Local rainfall is intimately tied to the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Local rainfall is a matter of the people's welfare.'

sentences.zh: 鶚元何得含混入告？

translations.literal: How can Eyuan mingle truth and falsehood in his reports?
translations.idiomatic: How can Eyuan blur the truth in his reports?'

sentences.zh: 」尋奏請截漕十萬石，淮、徐、海三府州被災較重，碾米治賑，如所議行。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized requesting diversion of one hundred thousand shi of tribute grain; the three prefectures and departments of Huai, Xu, and Hai had suffered more heavily, and rice was to be husked for relief—as deliberated, it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he asked to divert 100,000 shi of tribute grain, mill it, and use it for relief in the harder-hit Huai, Xu, and Hai districts. The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，高郵巡檢陳倚道察知書吏偽印重徵，知州吳瑍置不問；

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year Gaoyou sub-prefectural inspector Chen Yidao detected that clerks had used forged seals to levy extra taxes; Prefect Wu Yin took no action;
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 Gaoyou inspector Chen Yidao discovered that clerks had used forged seals to levy extra taxes; Prefect Wu Yin ignored it;

sentences.zh: 牒上，鶚元亦置不問，揭報戶部。

translations.literal: when the report was forwarded upward, Eyuan also took no action and merely forwarded it to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: when the report reached Eyuan, he too ignored it and merely forwarded it to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上諮鶚元，鶚元猶庇瑍不以實陳，乃遣尚書慶桂、侍郎王昶按治；

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Eyuan; Eyuan still shielded Yin and did not report truthfully, whereupon Minister Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang were dispatched to investigate;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Eyuan, who still shielded Yin and did not tell the truth. The emperor then sent Minister Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang to investigate;

sentences.zh: 責鶚元欺罔，奪官，逮鶚元等下刑部治罪。

translations.literal: Eyuan was rebuked for deception, stripped of office, and Eyuan and others were arrested and handed to the Board of Punishments for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Eyuan was condemned for deceit, stripped of rank, and arrested with his associates for trial by the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福崧劾鶚元得句容知縣王光陛牒發糧書侵挪錢糧，但令江寧府察覈。

translations.literal: Governor Fusong impeached Eyuan for receiving a dispatch from Jurong Magistrate Wang Guangbi exposing grain clerks' embezzlement of funds and grain, yet only ordering Jiangning Prefecture to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fusong also accused Eyuan of receiving a report from Jurong magistrate Wang Guangbi exposing grain clerks' embezzlement, yet referring it only to Jiangning prefecture for review.

sentences.zh: 上責鶚元玩視民瘼，徇情骫法，命置重典。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for treating the people's suffering lightly and bending the law out of personal favor, ordering severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor condemned Eyuan for neglecting the people's welfare and bending the law out of favoritism, and ordered severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 獄具，擬斬立決，命改監候。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, immediate decapitation was recommended; the emperor ordered commutation to imprisonment awaiting autumn review.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict recommended immediate execution; the emperor commuted the sentence to imprisonment pending review.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，釋還裡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was released and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1791 he was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1797.

sentences.zh: 論曰：法者所以持天下之平。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Law is what upholds fairness under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Law exists to uphold fairness in the realm.

sentences.zh: 人君馭群臣，既知其不肖，乃以一日之愛憎喜怒，屈法以從之，此非細故也。

translations.literal: When a ruler governs his ministers, having already known their unworthiness, yet bends the law to follow a day's love, hatred, joy, or anger—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler already knows his ministers are unworthy yet bends the law to suit a passing mood of affection, anger, joy, or resentment, the consequences are grave.

sentences.zh: 焯、阿思哈、景素坐貪皆勘實，猶尚復起；

translations.literal: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of greed with substantiated investigations, yet were still restored;
translations.idiomatic: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of corruption on solid evidence, yet were restored to office;

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿匿災至面謾，反誅告者；

translations.literal: Tu Erbing'a concealed disaster to the point of deceiving the emperor face to face, yet those who reported it were punished instead;
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbing'a concealed a disaster even to the emperor's face, yet those who reported it were punished;

sentences.zh: 兆麟口給，鶚元迎上指，至不勝疆政而始去之。

translations.literal: Zhaolin was glib of tongue, Eyuan courted the emperor's intent—only when they could no longer bear frontier governance were they removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin was glib, Eyuan read the emperor's mind—only when they proved unfit for frontier rule were they finally removed.

sentences.zh: 高宗常謂：「朕非甚懦弱姑息之主，不能執法。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor often said: 'I am not a very weak and indulgent ruler who cannot enforce the law.'
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor often said: 'I am not so weak and indulgent that I cannot enforce the law.'

sentences.zh: 」執法固難，自克其愛憎喜怒，尤不易言也。

translations.literal: Enforcing the law is indeed difficult; to master one's own love, hatred, joy, and anger is even harder to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Enforcing the law is hard enough; mastering one's own passions is harder still.'
